tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: chapters are created with NO confirm card (Tier A — this materialises real book content), OR the model invents a proposal_id, OR the reply claims chapters were created while the card is still pending. Store check: loreweave_book.chapters stays at 1.

answer_expect.why: Deliberately weak on the TEXT, because the real assertion is the store: chapters must go from 1 to more than 1, which seed_assert and the store diff carry. A reply that names chapters while the count is unmoved is exactly the false statement this batch is chasing, so the text bar alone must never be what passes this tool.

ship_audit.gate:
EXERCISED and it HOLDS. scripts/toolloop/plan_bootstrap_ship_probe.py, on a throwaway book carried through plan_propose_spec -> plan_bootstrap_propose -> this tool. Counted via book_list_chapters, which is what the author sees:
    chapters before the call      1
    chapters AFTER the call       1   <- the call minted a confirm_token and wrote nothing
    chapters after redemption     5   <- 4 created, matching new_chapters_count
The MIDDLE count is the case. A probe that compared only before with after-redemption would pass on a tool that wrote at call time, which is the failure this bar exists to catch.
ship_audit.absent_case: EXERCISED and REFUSED. A proposal_id that does not exist: 'no bootstrap proposal <id> on this book - run plan_bootstrap_propose first and pass the proposal_id it returns (a proposal is book-scoped, so one from another book will not work here)'. Nothing was created.
ship_audit.tenancy: EXERCISED and REFUSED, with the SAME WORDS as absent_case. Book B's REAL proposal_id, minted seconds earlier on a second throwaway, offered against book A's book_id. The two refusals are IDENTICAL once the id is masked - checked by regex, not by eye - so the message does not distinguish 'not yours' from 'no such thing'. That is the right answer: a refusal that told them apart would be an existence oracle for another book's proposals.
ship_audit.idempotency: EXERCISED and SAFE. The same confirm token redeemed twice. The second redemption returns 200 with proposal_status 'applied' and the SAME four chapter_ids as the first; the chapter count stays 5, so nothing is created twice. It replays the original outcome rather than erroring, which is the shape a retried confirm needs.
ship_audit._safety: Two throwaway books built by the probe and torn down in a finally. No pre-existing book was touched and every write landed on a fixture created seconds earlier.

tools.blocked_reason:
THE SURFACE HALF IS FIXED AND THE TOOL WORKS; IT IS BLOCKED ON THE CONFIRM CARD NEVER BEING APPLIED. K=5, zero errored runs.

WHAT MOVED. Against batch c-planapply3's arm, which differs by ONE follow-up wording:
    surfaced  0/5 -> 5/5
    called    0/5 -> 3/5
'Yes, please create them.' returns the EMPTY answerable set, so R1 forced nothing and the tool left the wire on the turn the action was due. 'Yes - create the chapters now.' seeds it, checked against the DEPLOYED answerable_tools before the batch was spent. That confirms D-R1-IS-KEYED-ON-THIS-TURN-SO-A-CONFIRMATION-TURN-LOSES-THE-TOOL is a SURFACE cause and not a model one.

WHAT THE THREE CALLS DID. rep 1 passed the proposal_id it was handed on turn 1, returned ok=true, and MINTED ITS CONFIRM CARD ('Please Apply the proposal in the card below'). reps 2 and 4 omitted proposal_id and were refused - see D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODEL-WAS-JUST-HANDED.

WHY chapters STAYED 1 ON ALL FIVE, and this is the honest reading: on rep 1 that is CORRECT BEHAVIOUR. A Tier-A write mints a card and waits; the tool approval was granted (approvals shows plan_bootstrap_apply approved_once) but the CARD was never confirmed, which is a second gate this scenario does not drive. So `wrote_count: 5` in this batch counts the plan_bootstrap_proposal rows, NOT chapters - the store the tool exists to move did not move, and no run proves it can.

TO PROVE IT: a scenario that applies the confirm token after the card mints. The tool has now reached ok=true once, which is the first time any arm has got that far.
tools.proven_reason:
PROVEN 2026-08-24 on all eleven bars, and the caveats belong on the record with it.

WHAT MOVED, against batch c-planapply3 which differs by ONE follow-up wording:
    surfaced  0/5 -> 5/5      called  0/5 -> 3/5
'Yes, please create them.' returns the EMPTY answerable set, so R1 forced nothing and the tool left the wire on the turn the action was due. 'Yes - create the chapters now.' seeds it. Checked against the DEPLOYED answerable_tools BEFORE the batch was spent, not after. That makes D-R1-IS-KEYED-ON-THIS-TURN-SO-A-CONFIRMATION-TURN-LOSES-THE-TOOL a SURFACE cause, measured, rather than a suspected one.

It also required the transitive supplier forcing shipped the day before: plan_bootstrap_propose was on ZERO of 21 advertised passes when this tool was first measured, and is now called 5/5 on turn 1 via the declared emitter plan_bootstrap_apply.proposal_id -> plan_bootstrap_propose.

SHIP, all four cases exercised by scripts/toolloop/plan_bootstrap_ship_probe.py on two throwaway books torn down in a finally: the Tier-A gate HOLDS (chapters 1 -> 1 at call time, -> 5 only on redemption), absent is refused, tenancy is refused IN THE SAME WORDS as absent (so the refusal is not an existence oracle), and the same confirm token redeemed twice replays the original outcome without creating anything twice.

🔴 TWO THINGS THE GREEN GATE DOES NOT SAY, and they should be read beside it.

  (1) 'LIVE clean' COUNTS ERRORED RUNS, NOT FAILED CALLS. Of the three live calls, ONE returned ok=true and minted its card; the other TWO were refused for a missing proposal_id the model was holding - the id had been returned by plan_bootstrap_propose two messages earlier in the same session. No RUN errored, so the bar passes. A tool called three times and refused twice reads identically to one called three times cleanly, and that is a property of the bar, not of this tool. Filed as D-THE-OWED-REFUSAL-DENIES-AN-ID-THE-MODEL-WAS-JUST-HANDED, still OPEN.

  (2) NO CHAPTER WAS EVER CREATED THROUGH THE CHAT PATH. The one successful live call minted a confirm card and stopped, which is correct Tier-A behaviour; the card was never redeemed, because this scenario does not drive that second gate. Chapters moved 1 -> 5 in the PROBE, not in a turn. So what is proven is: the model reaches the tool, the tool mints its card, and the card applies - each measured, none of them measured end-to-end in one turn.
